facts.fact: The Gemini API is a Google AI offering whose docs now live under https://aistudio.google.com/docs/* (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

As of 2026-11-14, Gemini API docs URLs https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/* return 301 redirects to https://aistudio.google.com/docs/* (for example /docs/billing, /docs/rate-limits, /docs/api-key, /docs/terms) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)

The Gemini API docs publish https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt, which lists markdown pages such as https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key.md and links the full corpus at https://aistudio.google.com/llms-full.txt (https://aistudio.google.com/llms.txt)
Each Gemini API key belongs to a Google Cloud project, which holds billing, collaborators and permissions (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)

New AI Studio users get a default Google Cloud project and Gemini API key, while users with existing Cloud accounts must import their projects into AI Studio before creating keys there (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)

Gemini API tiers, rate limits and spend caps are set per Cloud Billing account, not per project; projects linked to that billing account inherit its tier and unlinking billing returns a project to the free tier (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

To enable paid Gemini API use, select the free-tier project in AI Studio, click "Set up billing" in the Billing Tier column, choose or create a Cloud Billing account, and prepay a minimum of $5 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)
The Google Agentspace experience and default app were renamed Gemini Enterprise on 2025-10-09 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise docs at https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise/docs/* redirect (301) to https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/*, and pages also have .md.txt variants such as /docs/editions.md.txt (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs)
Gemini Enterprise Business edition covers 1-500 users with 25 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Standard edition covers 1 or more users with 30 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Plus edition covers 1 or more users with 75 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Pay-as-you-go edition starts at a 1-seat minimum (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Gemini Enterprise Frontline edition requires 150 or more Standard or Plus users and has 2 GiB pooled index storage per user (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

Gemini Enterprise Pay-as-you-go edition has been GA since 2026-08-01 and was opened to all invoiced Cloud Billing accounts in September 2026 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise Business edition is a web SaaS app at business.gemini.google.com; admins do not need Google Cloud console access and there are no project numbers or project-level IAM roles to manage (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

Gemini Enterprise Standard, Plus and Pay-as-you-go subscriptions are purchased per Cloud Billing account in the Cloud console on Gemini Enterprise > Plans & billing (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)

Console-purchased Gemini Enterprise seat subscriptions have a seat cap, and larger orders go through Google Cloud sales (offline order or allowlist exemption) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)

Gemini Enterprise admin setup sequence: create or select a Cloud project, confirm billing, buy edition licenses, assign licenses (manual by email or automatic at first sign-in), grant Gemini Enterprise Admin and User roles, connect the identity provider, then create Google and third-party data stores (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/before-you-begin.md.txt)

Gemini Enterprise licenses are distributed to a specific project and location (global, us, eu, in-country), so a user needing two multi-regions needs two licenses (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)
Gemini Enterprise license distribution and reclaim in the console has been GA since 2026-06-25 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Unlicensed Gemini Enterprise users have no access: removing a license ends access immediately, and on early subscription termination licenses enter a one-week deactivating grace period (GA 2026-03-17) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)
NotebookLM Enterprise was renamed Gemini Notebook Enterprise on 2026-07-16 with unchanged API endpoints (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Notebook Enterprise is sold standalone or as part of Gemini Enterprise, and notebooks are shared across both apps in the same project and location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

Jules in Pro and Ultra (Google AI Pro / Ultra) are available only to individual @gmail.com accounts (https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits)

Day-one engagement asks: the Cloud project and billing account used for Gemini API or Gemini Enterprise; a Gemini Enterprise license plus roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser (builder) or roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin (admin); the identity provider and location (global/us/eu) of the Gemini Enterprise app; and for Workspace API work a service account or OAuth client plus a super admin to authorize domain-wide delegation (unverified) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control ; https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)
Gemini API standard keys tie requests to a Cloud project for billing and quota but do not identify the caller (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini API authorization (auth) keys are bound to a Google Cloud service account and run requests under that identity (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini API auth keys are restricted to the Generative Language API by default and support fast enforcement against leaked keys (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
All newly created AI Studio keys are auth keys from 2026-05-28 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini API keys created in the Cloud console must each be bound to a service account (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Unrestricted Gemini API standard keys must be restricted to the Gemini API, which needs the apikeys.keys.update permission (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
The Gemini API rejects unrestricted standard keys, and from 2026-05-07 long-dormant unrestricted keys are blocked and show a "Blocked" tag in AI Studio (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Creating a Gemini API key requires Cloud IAM permissions such as apikeys.keys.create and iam.serviceAccounts.create (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Creating a Gemini API key requires iam.serviceAccounts.create among its Cloud IAM permissions (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)
Gemini client libraries read the key from GEMINI_API_KEY or GOOGLE_API_KEY, and if both are set GOOGLE_API_KEY wins (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/api-key)

facts.fact: The Gemini Developer API uses a Gemini API key, unlike the Cloud Gemini platform (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/migrate-to-cloud)
The Cloud Gemini platform (Vertex AI, docs slug gemini-enterprise-agent-platform) uses Cloud service accounts and IAM rather than Gemini API keys (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/migrate-to-cloud)

The google-genai SDK switches to the Cloud platform with genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=..., location=...) or genai.Client(enterprise=True, ...) for the Interactions API (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/migrate-to-cloud)

Gemini Enterprise supports Google Identity, which Google recommends and which is GA for third-party data stores since 2026-08-20 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise supports Workforce Identity Federation (Entra ID, Okta, AD FS, generic OIDC/SAML 2.0) for third-party-only setups (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Gemini Enterprise Microsoft 365 ingestion (SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook) requires Entra ID via Workforce Identity Federation (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

For Gemini Enterprise, create the workforce identity pool in global even for us/eu apps and map google.subject to the lowercase email, not the Entra object ID (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)
Entra group claims for Gemini Enterprise must be filtered, with limits of 150 groups for SAML and 200 for OIDC (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

The Gemini Enterprise identity provider is set per location at Gemini Enterprise > Settings > Authentication > Add identity provider for global, us or eu, with one IdP type per location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Changing the Gemini Enterprise IdP type or pool requires recreating data stores and resets user IDs, losing chat history (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Gemini Enterprise uses SCIM with Entra ID or Okta for large group sets and user/group autocomplete; Okta SCIM autocomplete for sharing notebooks and agents is GA since 2026-08-20 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Programmatic Gemini Enterprise API access uses Application Default Credentials (gcloud auth application-default login) or bearer tokens from gcloud auth print-access-token, or attached service accounts on Google Cloud (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Gemini Enterprise API access supports service account impersonation, which needs the Service Account Token Creator role (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Service account impersonation for Gemini Enterprise API calls requires the Service Account Token Creator role (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Gemini Enterprise API access supports workload identity federation from on-premises or other clouds (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)

gcloud auth application-default login sets up ADC and gcloud auth print-access-token prints a bearer token for Gemini Enterprise API calls (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/authentication)
Gemini Enterprise admins can view an agent's identity, typically a SPIFFE ID (Preview 2026-04-21) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Registering an ADK agent in Gemini Enterprise that accesses Google resources as the user requires a Web application OAuth client with redirect URIs https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/oauth-redirect and https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/static/oauth/oauth.html (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

An ADK agent acting on behalf of users in Gemini Enterprise has its OAuth client stored as an authorizations resource (serverSideOauth2) with access_type=offline and prompt=consent (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

Workspace APIs accept OAuth client IDs (Web, Android, iOS, Chrome Extension, Desktop, TV/limited input) with user consent, API keys for public data only, and service accounts (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)
Workspace APIs accept service account credentials (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Each Workspace OAuth client type has an optional "Use this client for an AI-powered agent" checkbox for apps acting on behalf of users; it cannot be changed after creation, and Google advises separate clients for agent and standard features (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Cloud IAM roles do not grant Workspace data: a service account reaches Workspace data only by being shared on files, being assigned a Workspace admin role, or via domain-wide delegation (https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Workspace domain-wide delegation is authorised by a super admin at Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls > Manage Domain Wide Delegation > Add new, entering the service account or OAuth client ID and comma-delimited scopes (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-api-access-with-domain-wide-delegation)

With multi-party approval another super admin must approve domain-wide delegation, and changes take up to 24 hours (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-api-access-with-domain-wide-delegation ; https://developers.google.com/workspace/guides/create-credentials)

Gemini CLI auth modes are Sign in with Google (recommended locally), Gemini API key (GEMINI_API_KEY), or Vertex AI via ADC (gcloud auth application-default login), a service account key (GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS) or a Cloud API key (GOOGLE_API_KEY) with GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)
Gemini CLI can authenticate with a Gemini API key set in GEMINI_API_KEY (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)
Gemini CLI can use Vertex AI via ADC (gcloud auth application-default login) (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)
Gemini CLI auth settings can live in .gemini/.env (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)

facts.fact: Company, school and Workspace accounts (including Google AI Ultra for Business) using Gemini CLI generally must set GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT, enable the Gemini for Cloud API and have IAM permissions; headless mode reuses cached credentials or env-var auth (https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/authentication/)

Gemini Notebook Enterprise supports Cloud Identity or third-party IdPs (Entra ID, Okta, Ping, PingFederate, other OIDC/SAML 2.0) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)
Gemini Notebook Enterprise sharing is limited to users in the same Cloud project and public sharing is disallowed (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin (Gemini Enterprise Admin) grants Discovery Engine Editor plus admin-only permissions such as setting agent IAM policies (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser (Gemini Enterprise User) allows creating, updating and deleting agents and using apps (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceRestrictedUser gives no Gemini Enterprise app access unless the user is also granted agentspaceUser per app (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

Gemini Enterprise predefined IAM roles are roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin, roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser, roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceRestrictedUser, roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceViewer, roles/discoveryengine.editor and roles/discoveryengine.viewer (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
The Gemini Enterprise Admin and User IAM role names became available 2026-04-15 and map to the existing Discovery Engine role IDs (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

To create agents in Agent Gallery / Workflow Builder a user needs roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceUser (project-level, or per-app with agentspaceRestrictedUser at project level) plus a Gemini Enterprise license (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
Creating agents in Agent Gallery / Workflow Builder requires a Gemini Enterprise license (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

Only roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin holds discoveryengine.agents.setIamPolicy, while agentspaceUser can only propose agent IAM changes (agentIamProposals) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

Registering an ADK agent in Gemini Enterprise requires Gemini Enterprise Admin (roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin), the Discovery Engine API enabled and an existing app (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)
An ADK agent registered in Gemini Enterprise must be hosted on Agent Runtime in a matching location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

Each Gemini Enterprise agent registration consumes the daily agent-creation quota, which scales with distributed licenses (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/register-and-manage-an-adk-agent)

Gemini Enterprise admins get roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin plus Service Usage Consumer and Logs Viewer, typically granted by a project owner (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
Distributing Gemini Enterprise licenses needs roles/billing.admin on the Cloud Billing account (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/licenses)
The Discovery Engine service agent needs roles/discoveryengine.serviceAgent on the project for Gemini Enterprise app creation (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)

If the Discovery Engine service agent lacks roles/discoveryengine.serviceAgent, Gemini Enterprise app creation fails with "Internal error encountered (Code 13)" (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/access-control)
Gemini Enterprise app-level IAM policies are GA since 2026-02-02 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise introduced granular resource-level Admin, Viewer and User roles for apps and data stores on 2026-09-28 and supports custom IAM roles for AI developer tools since 2026-08-18 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise agent sharing is GA since 2026-02-23 (direct, Google Groups, Workforce Identity Federation pools, configurable admin review) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Only Gemini Enterprise Admins can transfer ownership of shared agents (since 2026-09-21) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Users request Google Cloud Marketplace agents from the Gemini Enterprise Agent Gallery and an administrator reviews them; approved agents appear under "From your organization" (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/agent-gallery.md.txt)
Gemini Enterprise Frontline users can only use agents an admin provisions and cannot create custom skills (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

Gemini Enterprise Agent Designer (GA 2026-01-12) was renamed Workflow Builder at its GA on 2026-09-03, with an enhanced Agent Gallery (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Signing in to Gemini Notebook Enterprise requires roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmUser (Cloud NotebookLM User) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmOwner (Cloud NotebookLM Admin) is the admin role for Gemini Notebook Enterprise, alongside UI-granted roles/discoveryengine.notebookOwner, notebookEditor and notebookViewer (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

In Gemini Notebook Enterprise, roles containing discoveryengine.notebooks.get at project level expose every notebook (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/overview)

facts.fact: Optional project-level Gemini API spend caps on the AI Studio Spend page can be set by users with the editor, owner or admin role (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

Turning the Workspace Gemini app on or off needs the Gemini Settings admin privilege, at Admin console > Generative AI > Gemini app > Service status, scoped by OU or configuration group (group overrides OU) (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)
The Workspace Gemini app "User access" setting can allow all users regardless of license (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)

Controlling third-party app access to Workspace data at Admin console > Security > Access and data control > API controls needs the Service Settings admin privilege (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-which-apps-access-google-workspace-data)

Workspace API controls offer per-app levels Trusted, Specific Google data, Limited and Blocked; services can be set Restricted (revoking untrusted tokens); unconfigured third-party apps can be allowed, limited to basic sign-in, or blocked (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/apps/control-which-apps-access-google-workspace-data)

For Gemini API Unpaid Services, Google uses submitted content and responses to provide, improve and develop products and ML technologies, and human reviewers may read them (disconnected from account, key and project), so sensitive data should not be submitted (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)

Gemini API Paid Services prompts and responses are not used to improve products, are processed under a Data Processing Addendum, and are logged for a limited time only for abuse detection, safety and legal needs (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)
AI Studio counts as Gemini API Paid Services when tied to a billed project or Workspace account (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

Gemini API users in the EEA, Switzerland or UK get Paid Services data terms on all services, and API clients offered to users there may use only Paid Services; terms effective 2026-03-23, and users must be 18+ (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)
Gemini API Paid Services data may be stored or cached in any country where Google or its agents have facilities (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)
Because Gemini API paid data may be stored anywhere, data residency requires the Cloud platform (Vertex AI) instead of the Gemini API (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/terms)

Gemini Enterprise locations are multi-regions global, us and eu (Google recommends global) plus in-country regions GA with allowlist: Brazil br (2026-10-28), Canada ca, India in, Japan asia-northeast1, Singapore sg, UK europe-west2 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Gemini Enterprise regional API hosts are us-discoveryengine.googleapis.com and eu-discoveryengine.googleapis.com (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)

Gemini Enterprise base functionality supports at-rest data residency and ML processing in us, eu and in-country regions, while global has no regional residency (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)

In Gemini Enterprise several models (for example Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini 3.7 Flash) are global-only, and enabling an unsupported model routes traffic to global (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)
In Gemini Enterprise, Grounding with Google Search is global-only (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)

VPC Service Controls, CMEK (US/EU multi-regions only, not global), Access Transparency and data residency are supported for Gemini Enterprise Standard/Plus and Gemini Notebook Enterprise, except when Grounding with Google Search is enabled (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/compliance-security-controls)

Gemini Enterprise lists HIPAA, FedRAMP, ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS and BSI C5:2020 certifications (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/compliance-security-controls)
Antigravity in Gemini Enterprise is excluded from Access Transparency, FedRAMP, IL4/IL5, ISO, ITAR and SOC (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/compliance-security-controls)
Model Armor can screen prompts and responses in Gemini Enterprise apps and Gemini Notebook Enterprise (since 2025-09-15) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Model Armor for Gemini Enterprise is not available in the global location (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/locations)
Governance of Gemini Enterprise agents and MCP servers through Agent Registry and Agent Gateway is GA since 2026-06-25 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Agent Gateway governs Gemini Enterprise agents and MCP servers together with Agent Registry, GA since 2026-06-25 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise custom MCP server data stores are off by default behind an organization policy constraint (2026-04-28), and managed org policy constraints for allowed data sources and egress FQDNs went GA 2026-07-06/07 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Gemini Enterprise ingestion connectors enforce source ACLs by combining an identity sync (users to groups, every 30 minutes to 7 days) and a full sync (content to groups) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/introduction-to-connectors-and-data-stores)

Gemini Enterprise federated connectors query the source live and send the query string to third-party backends (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/introduction-to-connectors-and-data-stores)

facts.fact: Each Gemini Enterprise document supports up to 3,000 readers, and access control can only be chosen at data store creation (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)
Gemini Enterprise Cloud Storage, BigQuery and custom sources need explicit ACLs or external identity mapping (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/configure-identity-provider)

Gemini Enterprise audit logs appear under protoPayload.serviceName="discoveryengine.googleapis.com": Admin Activity for configuration and IAM changes, and Data Access (must be enabled) for Search, StreamAssist and similar (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/audit-logging)
Gemini Enterprise usage audit logs of user queries and responses in Cloud Logging are GA since 2026-02-04 (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)
Gemini Enterprise admins can configure the chat retention period (GA 2026-03-11) (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

In Workspace, customer prompts and content are not used to train generative AI models outside the domain without permission, Gemini app and Gemini Notebook chats are not human-reviewed without permission, and Gemini only accesses content the user can already see (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)

Most Workspace Business, Enterprise, Essentials, Frontline and Nonprofits editions (and AI Expanded Access) get the Gemini app as a core service with enterprise data protections, while Business Base, Essentials Starter, Cloud Identity, Workspace Individual and others get it as an additional service under consumer terms where chats may be human-reviewed (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)
Gemini in Workspace prompts are kept 90 days to indefinitely (admin-set) (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)
Workspace Gemini app history is kept 3, 18 (default) or 36 months, or up to 72 hours with history off (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/turn-the-gemini-app-on-or-off)
Gemini Notebook does not retain prompts after the session (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)

Workspace Gemini certifications: SOC 1/2/3, ISO 9001, 27001, 27701, 27017, 27018, 42001, FedRAMP High (Gemini in Workspace apps and Gemini app) and HIPAA (Gemini in Workspace) (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)
Gemini Notebook and Gemini in Chrome are not covered by ISO, SOC, FedRAMP or the HIPAA BAA (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)

Workspace data regions at Admin console > Data > Compliance > Data regions (Data Regions Settings admin privilege) offer United States, Europe or No preference on qualifying Business/Enterprise/Frontline/Education editions (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/compliance/choose-a-geographic-location-for-your-data)

The Workspace data regions page does not state Gemini coverage, and Workspace data-region settings do not apply to Gemini Notebook data (https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/compliance/choose-a-geographic-location-for-your-data ; https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/gemini/generative-ai-in-google-workspace-privacy-hub)
Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise both list IP indemnification (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview)
Gemini Code Assist Enterprise adds IP indemnification plus code customization from GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/codeassist/overview)

Gemini API prices are USD per 1M input and output tokens (output includes thinking tokens), some media per image or per second/minute, and Grounding with Google Search per 1,000 requests; Flex and Priority tiers exist (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
The Gemini Batch API is 50% off standard prices (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Gemini 3.8 Flash costs $0.75 input / $3.75 output per 1M tokens through 2026-12-31 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Gemini 3.8 Flash rises to $1.50 input / $7.50 output per 1M tokens from 2027-01-01 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview costs $2.00 input / $12.00 output per 1M tokens with no free tier (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)
Grounding with Google Search for Gemini 3+ includes 5,000 free requests per month, then $14 per 1,000 (shown 2026-11-14) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/pricing)

Gemini API usage tiers (shown 2026-11-14): Free (no billing); Tier 1 (linked billing, $250 monthly cap); Tier 2 ($100 paid and 3 days since first payment, $2,000 cap); Tier 3 ($1,000 paid and 30 days, $20,000-$100,000+ cap) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing ; https://aistudio.google.com/docs/rate-limits)

Gemini API rate limits are per project and cover RPM, input TPM, RPD (reset midnight Pacific), plus IPM/TPD for some models and a rolling 10-minute spend limit ($10 Tier 1, $200 Tier 2/3); paid tiers can request increases (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/rate-limits)
Exceeding any Gemini API rate limit returns 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/rate-limits)

facts.fact: Gemini API Prepay and Postpay plans exist from 2026-03-23, with new users defaulting to Prepay ($5 minimum, $5,000 maximum, credits expire after 12 months) (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)
On Gemini API Prepay, at a $0 balance all keys in linked projects fail with HTTP 402 (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)
Google Cloud accounts opened after 2026-03-02 cannot use the $300 Welcome credit for Gemini API or AI Studio (https://aistudio.google.com/docs/billing)

Gemini Enterprise Business, Standard, Plus and Frontline are seat subscriptions, while the Pay-as-you-go edition and "Pay-as-you-go usage above quota" (renamed from "Overages" 2026-10-06) bill usage (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes)

Partner models Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are pay-as-you-go in Gemini Enterprise, and seat credits cover only first-party Gemini models (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is a pay-as-you-go partner model in Gemini Enterprise not covered by seat credits (https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/editions)

Third-party sources report Gemini Enterprise Business at $21 per seat per month and Standard/Plus from $30 per seat per month (secondary) (https://dupple.com/learn/gemini-enterprise-pricing ; https://coworker.ai/blog/gemini-enterprise-pricing)
The official Gemini Enterprise pricing URL https://cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise/pricing returned 404 on 2026-11-14 (secondary) (https://dupple.com/learn/gemini-enterprise-pricing)

Google Workspace is billed per user per month (shown 2026-11-14): Business Starter $7.00, Standard $14.00, Plus $22.00 (monthly billing; 50% promo for new customers from 2026-11-27 to 2027-02-27 on the first 20 users); Enterprise via sales; AI Expanded Access is a separate add-on (https://workspace.google.com/pricing)
Jules usage limits: Base 15 tasks per rolling 24 hours and 3 concurrent; Pro 100 and 15; Ultra 300 and 60 (https://jules.google/docs/usage-limits)
